statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-54874 ("Excessive Memory Use Buffering DTLS Records for a Future Epoch", Low): while a DTLS handshake is in progress, OpenSSL buffers records that arrive early for the next epoch, and each buffered record kept the whole read buffer it arrived in (about 16 kilobytes) instead of only its own bytes, so a peer sending small forged next-epoch records can make an OpenSSL DTLS endpoint retain about 1.7 megabytes per connection. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.8; the advisory states that no FIPS modules are affected because the affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260825.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/4808b5d64176451f3d93d87d0ac9c81a9b13fb23, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.8. Alpine fixed it in openssl 3.5.8-r0: https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-54874. The published DHI Alpine 3.23 builds from the openssl source (the main repository packages, and the openssl-fips FIPS-provider package in the DHI enterprise repository, built from the same source at matching versions from 3.5.5_git20260330-r1 on) are 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2, each on x86_64 and aarch64. The libcrypto in every one of these builds reports the OpenSSL release of its package version (3.5.5_git20260330-r1, a git snapshot dated 30 March 2026, reports 3.5.5). Builds before 3.5.8-r0 are based on OpenSSL 3.5.7 or earlier, and 3.5.8-r0 and every later build on OpenSSL 3.5.8 or later. The fix copies only the record's own bytes into the queue instead of taking over the read buffer and setting up a new one with tls_setup_read_buffer(); the compiler inlines the changed function into dtls_get_more_records() in libssl. Using that function's address from the shipped debug symbols, the disassembly of libssl shows two calls from dtls_get_more_records() to tls_setup_read_buffer() in 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0 and 3.5.7-r1, and one in 3.5.8-r0 and every later build, on both architectures (debug symbols from the openssl-dbg package of each build). The openssl-fips package holds only the FIPS provider (fips.so, built from the same OpenSSL release as the package version in every build on both architectures) and its configuration files; the DTLS record layer is in libssl.

Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, DSA-6465-1: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-54874. The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds, and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build, only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64: 25 versions, 17 standard and 8 FIPS builds, based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. No build based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1 or 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-54874. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, the fixed boundary here, and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u2 entry naming it. The fix copies only the record's own bytes into the queue instead of taking over the read buffer and setting up a new one with tls_setup_read_buffer(); the compiler inlines the changed function into dtls_get_more_records() in libssl. Using that function's address from the shipped debug symbols, the disassembly of libssl shows two calls from dtls_get_more_records() to tls_setup_read_buffer() in every build before the first rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, and one in that build and every later build, FIPS builds included, on both architectures (debug symbols from the libssl3t64-dbgsym package of each build). Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the build's own OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory places the affected code outside the FIPS module boundary, and the FIPS builds' libcrypto and libssl are Debian's 3.5 libraries checked above.
